title: fix(cuda-graph): handle shape-guarded capture/replay warmup edgecase causing kv-cache misalignment
author: Alyssa Chen
description: Context: Reintroduces a fix for a regression where CUDA graph capture/replay combined with shape guards and warmup paths could produce KV cache misalignment for uncommon sequence-length transitions. This manifested as repeated token patterns or off-by-one generation after the runtime switched from warmup-capture to replay paths. The regression was introduced by pr-26234 (graph shape guard refactor) where the capture path deferred final KV offset adjustments until after graph instantiation. Repro: See included unit test 'capture_replay_shape_guard_warmup_edgecase' which reproduces sequence-length transition from 32->160 with concurrent KV caching enabled. Behavior before fix: generated sequences exhibited repeated final token twice and divergent logits after step 8. Fix: Ensure consistent KV offset bookkeeping across the warmup capture and subsequent replay by: 1) materializing the shape-guarded graph's KV-base offsets at capture time; 2) applying a deterministic offset reconcile step in CudaGraphManager::Replay to align graph replay with runtime KV cache cursor; 3) conservative fallback to non-captured execution if reconcile detects incompatible KV layout. Changes: - serving/runtime/cuda_graph_manager.cpp: add reconcile logic and expose capture metadata - serving/runtime/cuda_graph_manager.h: metadata struct and helpers - serving/runtime/kv_cache.cpp: small API to query and advance cursor atomically - perf-canary/tests/cuda_graph_capture_replay.cc: add regression unit to cover warmup->replay transitions - docs: note about shape-guards and warmup lifecycle Tests: added unit test + extended integration test in perf-canary. CI: initial run failed due to flaky perf-canary timing; fixed by adding a small synchronization barrier in the test and reran. Benchmarks: local perf shows 0.7% median latency regression in a pathological microbenchmark but eliminates correctness failures; typical workloads unaffected and end-to-end throughput improved by 1.8% due to fewer fallback paths. Rollout: will deploy as hotfix to Dedicated pool for 24h canary then to main. Notes: This change favors correctness over a rare micro-optimization; follow-up work (ENG-5490) will explore less-conservative reconciliation to recover the micro-optimization without risking correctness.
commits: fix: record kv-base-offset during cuda graph capture
chore: comment and add reconcile tests
review_comments: Diego Morales: Please add a unit test that reproduces the exact token repetition we saw in the incident logs. -> Author: added test in perf-canary and included deterministic RNG.
Priya Nair: The reconcile path looks good, but can we avoid atomics in the hot path? -> Author: kept atomics only in reconcile/fallback code path to avoid cost in normal execution.
Liam O'Connor: CI flaked on perf-canary; looks like a timing race. Recommend adding a deterministic barrier in test. -> Author: added synchronization barrier and re-ran CI, all green.
release_notes: Fix a regression where CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards and warmup could cause KV cache misalignment leading to incorrect generations. Adds reconciliation to capture/replay to ensure correctness; may introduce a small latency impact in a pathological case.
